CheckPlayerIn.title: CheckPlayerIn
CheckPlayerIn.description: Payload for the admin-triggered player verification probe.

ClaimOut.title: ClaimOut
ClaimOut.description: Response of ``POST /orders/claim`` — how many guest orders were migrated.

ClientHints.title: ClientHints
ClientHints.description:
Passive signals a browser can report about itself.

Every field is optional and every field is caller-supplied, so nothing here
is proof on its own — it is corroboration, and it is bounded in length so a
crafted payload cannot use the evidence table as storage. Deliberately no
canvas/font/audio probing: those identify a device across sites, which is a
different (and consent-bearing) activity from describing this one request.

CodeAccessIn.title: CodeAccessIn
CodeAccessIn.description: Request a fresh magic link to view a guest order's delivered codes.

CodeAdminOut.title: CodeAdminOut
CodeAdminOut.description: Admin-only listing row. Includes the decrypted code.

CostSyncResult.title: CostSyncResult
CostSyncResult.description:
Outcome of the on-save cost refresh.

Returned alongside the upsert response so the admin UI can flash
either "cost updated from $X.XX → $Y.YY" or a clear reason when we
couldn't pull a price (cache miss, unknown denom, etc).

CustomerOrderSummary.title: CustomerOrderSummary
CustomerOrderSummary.description: Compact order row for the customer-360 list. Full detail lives at /orders/{id}.

CustomerOverviewOut.title: CustomerOverviewOut
CustomerOverviewOut.description: Aggregated read-only view of a customer for the admin SPA's /customers/{id} page.

CustomerStatsOut.title: CustomerStatsOut
CustomerStatsOut.description: Aggregate counters for the customer header card.

CustomerTaskSummary.title: CustomerTaskSummary
CustomerTaskSummary.description: Open fulfilment task (pending / in_progress / failed) for this customer.

CustomerTransactionOut.title: CustomerTransactionOut
CustomerTransactionOut.description:
A ledger movement as the customer may see it.

Deliberately not :class:`TransactionOut`. That one carries ``actor`` —
``admin:<uuid>`` for a manual adjustment — and the whole of
``extra_metadata``, which holds the note an operator writes while the admin
UI tells them it is "видна в audit log". It reached the customer's history
instead.

The field names match ``TransactionOut`` so no client has to learn a second
shape; what changes is what is in them.

DashboardMargin.title: DashboardMargin
DashboardMargin.description:
What the window's revenue left us, beside the revenue itself.

USD-only by necessity: cost is recorded in USD on the SKU, while revenue is
charged per currency. ``pct`` is what makes the two comparable on one card.

DayBucket.title: DayBucket
DayBucket.description: One day in a sparkline series.

DeliveryOut.title: DeliveryOut
DeliveryOut.description: A delivery artifact as the customer sees it.

DenomImportIn.description: One supplier denomination to import as a SKU + mapping.

EvidencePackOut.title: EvidencePackOut
EvidencePackOut.description:
What gets handed to the acquirer when a transaction is disputed.

Shaped for that use: the capture, plus the order's full timeline, so the
answer to "when was this delivered and to whom" is one request rather than
an admin stitching screens together against a 5-day clock.

FaqCreate.title: FaqCreate
FaqCreate.description: Body of ``POST /admin/catalog/brands/{brand_id}/faqs``. Brand comes from the path.

FieldCheck.description:
Opts a form field into storefront player verification.

Present only on the player-id field. ``server_field`` names the sibling
field whose value is passed as the checker's ``server_id``; set it when
the product has a sibling server/zone field, leave unset otherwise.

FormField.title: FormField
FormField.description: One field of a product's form schema.

FulfillmentTaskListItemOut.title: FulfillmentTaskListItemOut
FulfillmentTaskListItemOut.description:
A task as it appears in a list — everything except the attempt log.

The log is unbounded: a task whose supplier order stays open polls its
status once a minute for as long as that lasts, and one task in
production carries 1641 attempts. A list showing only ``attempts_count``
has no use for them, so they are fetched on demand from
``GET /admin/fulfillment/attempts?task_id=…`` instead of riding along with
every row.

FulfillmentTaskOut.title: FulfillmentTaskOut
FulfillmentTaskOut.description: Admin view of a task — includes attempts.

OrderEvidenceOut.description: Admin-only view of one order's capture. Never returned on public routes.

OrderFailIn.title: OrderFailIn
OrderFailIn.description: Body for the admin "close this order as failed" action.

OrderItemAdminOut.title: OrderItemAdminOut
OrderItemAdminOut.description: Admin view of an order line — adds the internal supplier order id.

OrderItemDisplay.title: OrderItemDisplay
OrderItemDisplay.description:
What the customer/admin should see for this line.

Resolved from the SKU → product → brand chain at read time, so a renamed
product reflects in old orders too. For an at-purchase-time snapshot we'd
move this to a stored jsonb column — deferred until we hit the use case.

OrderItemIn.title: OrderItemIn
OrderItemIn.description: One line of a new-order request.

OrderItemOut.description: One line of an order response.

OrderOut.description: Full order response (matches list and detail).

OrderRefOut.title: OrderRefOut

Just enough to recognise an order: what was in it.

The first line's artwork, because that is what an operator remembers about
an order — not its id. An order with no items (a wallet deposit) has no
image and says so by omission.

PaymentAdminOut.title: PaymentAdminOut
PaymentAdminOut.description: Admin-side detail with the full attempt log.

PaymentAttemptOut.title: PaymentAttemptOut
PaymentAttemptOut.description: Single audit row exposed to admin.

PaymentOut.description: A payment as the customer / admin sees it.

PaymentTriageRow.title: PaymentTriageRow
PaymentTriageRow.description: One stuck-pending payment row for the triage screen.

PaymentWebhookOut.title: PaymentWebhookOut
PaymentWebhookOut.description: One row of the webhook audit table.

PayoutOut.title: PayoutOut
PayoutOut.description:
A withdrawal, as the partner sees it.

The card number is masked to its last four digits. The partner already
knows which card they typed, and a full PAN in a JSON response is a PAN in
a browser cache, a proxy log and a screenshot.

PlayerCheckIn.title: PlayerCheckIn
PlayerCheckIn.description: Storefront player-verification request (no charname — it's a lookup).

PlayerCheckOut.title: PlayerCheckOut
PlayerCheckOut.description:
Storefront player-verification result.

``status`` discriminates three outcomes so the storefront can message each
precisely:
  * ``valid``   — the id resolved; ``name`` is the account nickname.
  * ``invalid`` — the supplier answered but the id does not exist (the
    customer mistyped it). The storefront tells them the player isn't found.
  * ``error``   — a fault on our or the supplier's side (no mapping,
    unconfigured, upstream/network failure). The storefront shows a generic
    "couldn't check" and never blames the customer.

``openid`` is intentionally omitted — it's an internal G2B id and must not
leak to the storefront.

kind.description: One of brand_logo, brand_hero, product_image, sku_image, broadcast_media.

PreviewIn.description: A code and the cart it would apply to.

PreviewOut.title: PreviewOut
PreviewOut.description:
Whether the code applies, and what it would do to the total.

``reason`` is only set when ``applicable`` is false, and it is deliberately
coarse: a code that does not exist, one that is switched off, and one whose
partner is suspended all report ``unknown``. Telling them apart would make
this endpoint a lookup service for other people's promo codes.

The amounts are for display. The order is priced again when it is actually
created, so a code deactivated in between cannot be spent at the price
shown here.

ProductSummaryOut.description: Compact product representation for product lists.

The partner, and the codes they promote.

No ``password_hash``, and no ``admin_note`` — the second is an internal

Carries the identity fields the operator recognises a person by — avatar,

ProviderChainItemOut.description: One adapter in the admin chain, with live probes.

ProviderChainOut.title: ProviderChainOut
ProviderChainOut.description: Full admin view of every FX adapter.

ProviderIncidentsOut.description:

Mirrors ``admin.service.triage_payments``'s definitions exactly so the
numbers agree with the existing triage screen.

ProviderQuoteOut.title: ProviderQuoteOut
ProviderQuoteOut.description: One provider's attempt at one quote.

ProviderStatusOut.title: ProviderStatusOut
ProviderStatusOut.description: A payment provider slug the storefront may show, and whether it's usable.

RateOut.title: RateOut
RateOut.description: A single rate as returned by ``GET /api/v1/fx/rates``.

RateSettingIn.title: RateSettingIn
RateSettingIn.description:
Admin toggle + optional typed rate for one quote.

Bounded at the edge as well as in the service: the column is
``Numeric(20, 10)``, so an unbounded Decimal reaches Postgres as a 500
rather than a 422, and a pinned rate skips the pricing band by design
(ADR-0055) — this field deserves what checking it can get. The admin UI
asks for confirmation when the number is far from the live FX rate.

RatesOut.title: RatesOut
RatesOut.description: List of supported rates for the storefront.

RecentPaymentOut.title: RecentPaymentOut
RecentPaymentOut.description:
One payment row for the admin detail screen's recent list.

Deliberately narrow — id/order_id/status/amount/currency/created_at only.
Never include email/phone/user identifiers here (see AGENTS.md §9).

RecipientListOut.title: RecipientListOut
RecipientListOut.description: A page of :class:`RecipientOut` plus the total matching count.

RecipientOut.title: RecipientOut
RecipientOut.description:
One targeted recipient row.

``tg_chat_id`` is a Postgres ``bigint`` — serialized as a string (money-rule
for big ids) so it survives round-tripping through a JS ``number`` without
precision loss.

RegisterOut.title: RegisterOut
RegisterOut.description:
Response for ``POST /auth/register``.

Registration no longer opens a session: the account exists but is unusable
for password login until the emailed link is followed (``POST
/auth/verify-email``, which *does* open a session).

ReinviteOut.title: ReinviteOut
ReinviteOut.description:
A fresh set-password link, handed to the admin who asked for it.

Returned rather than only emailed so an admin can pass it on over whatever
channel actually reaches the partner — the case this exists for is "the
email never arrived".

ReviewOut.title: ReviewOut
ReviewOut.description:
A published review as shown on the public brand page.

``author_name`` is the reviewer's ``display_name`` or ``None`` — never the
email. The frontend localizes a generic label when it is ``None``.

SavedSegmentOut.title: SavedSegmentOut
SavedSegmentOut.description: One saved segment as returned to its owning admin.

SearchHit.title: SearchHit
SearchHit.description: One row in the search palette.

SearchOut.title: SearchOut
SearchOut.description: Grouped search results — one bucket per source.

SettleIn.title: SettleIn
SettleIn.description:
Body of admin's ``POST /admin/payments/{id}/settle``.

Both fields are mandatory: this endpoint asserts money arrived without a
provider saying so, and the audit trail is only worth anything if it records
*why* and *against which provider transaction*.

in_stock.title: In Stock
in_stock.description: False when the supplier has no codes left. The count itself is not exposed.

display_price.description: Localised price. Returned only when the request specifies a currency.

SkuPickerOut.title: SkuPickerOut
SkuPickerOut.description:
Compact SKU row tailored for the admin combobox.

Includes the parent product's display name so the picker can render a
self-explanatory row (``"PUBG Mobile · 60 UC"``) without a second
fetch.

SkuUpdate.title: SkuUpdate
SkuUpdate.description:
Body of ``PATCH /admin/catalog/skus/{id}``.

Most fields follow a "None means don't touch" convention. The
variable-amount block is the exception: ``variable_amount``,
``min_amount_usd``, ``max_amount_usd`` and ``rate_multiplier`` are each
applied independently in :func:`admin_service.update_sku` based on
whether the caller actually sent them (``model_fields_set``), not on
whether the value is ``None`` — sending one of the three amount fields
as JSON ``null`` clears it, same as omitting it would leave it alone.
This lets a partial edit like ``{"max_amount_usd": "1000"}`` against an
already-variable SKU apply on its own, and lets the SKU edit form send
``variable_amount: false`` with the three fields as ``null`` to clear
them. After merging, the *resulting* row is re-validated against
``ck_skus_variable_amount_complete`` (see
:func:`require_variable_amount_fields`) — the request body alone can't
tell whether a partial edit leaves an already-variable SKU complete.

StatsOut.title: StatsOut
StatsOut.description:
Earnings over a rolling window.

``period`` names the window and ``since`` says where it starts, because
"month" here means the last 30 days rather than the calendar month — see
``affiliate.panel`` for why.

SuccessRateOut.title: SuccessRateOut
SuccessRateOut.description:
Succeeded / failed / pending counts + success percentage for the window.

See ``provider_analytics`` module docstring for the exact status-bucket
mapping (in particular how ``refunded``/``partially_refunded`` are
treated as succeeded).

SupplierHealthOut.title: SupplierHealthOut
SupplierHealthOut.description:
Connectivity probe result for a supplier.

``available`` is the only required signal — everything else is best-effort
and may be ``None`` when the supplier didn't answer or is not configured.

SupplierMappingIn.title: SupplierMappingIn
SupplierMappingIn.description: Payload for upserting a SKU↔supplier mapping.

SupplierMappingOut.title: SupplierMappingOut
SupplierMappingOut.description: Mapping row as exposed by admin endpoints.

SupplierMappingUpsertOut.title: SupplierMappingUpsertOut
SupplierMappingUpsertOut.description:
Combined upsert response: the row that was saved plus the optional
cost-refresh outcome.

TelegramLinkOut.title: TelegramLinkOut
TelegramLinkOut.description: Telegram-link projection used in admin views.

TelegramWidgetIn.title: TelegramWidgetIn
TelegramWidgetIn.description:
Body of ``POST /auth/telegram/widget``.

Matches the JSON object Telegram's Login Widget posts to its ``data-onauth`` callback,
plus the ``hash`` field.

TranslationIn.title: TranslationIn
TranslationIn.description: One ``locale`` of a translation. Used for categories, brands, and products.

UserAdminOut.title: UserAdminOut
UserAdminOut.description: Admin-side user record with telegram and lifecycle fields.

UserOut.title: UserOut
UserOut.description: User profile returned to authenticated clients.

UserRefOut.title: UserRefOut
UserRefOut.description:
Just enough to draw a person: a face and a name.

The panel linked to profiles by raw UUID in seven places. An id says
nothing an operator can recognise, and every one of those call sites would
otherwise have to grow its own join.

VolumeRow.title: VolumeRow
VolumeRow.description: Payment volume for one currency within the analytics window.

WalletOverviewOut.title: WalletOverviewOut
WalletOverviewOut.description: A user's view of their own ledger: one balance per (kind, currency).

WalletTopUpIn.title: WalletTopUpIn
WalletTopUpIn.description: Body of ``POST /api/v1/wallet/topup``. Currency is derived from ``provider``.

WebhookTriageRow.title: WebhookTriageRow
WebhookTriageRow.description: One failed-webhook row for the triage screen.

yupay__modules__affiliate__schemas__Bala.title: BalanceOut
yupay__modules__affiliate__schemas__Bala.description:
Straight from the ledger.

``available`` is the only figure a withdrawal can draw on. ``held`` is
commission still inside its hold period; ``reserved`` is already claimed by
an open request.

yupay__modules__affiliate__schemas__Toke.title: TokensOut
yupay__modules__affiliate__schemas__Toke.description:
What a sign-in hands back.

No ``refresh_token`` field, deliberately. It rides an HttpOnly cookie
(ADR-0007), so a script on the page cannot read a 30-day session that can
move money out.

yupay__modules__auth__schemas__TokensOut.title: TokensOut
yupay__modules__auth__schemas__TokensOut.description:
Response for any endpoint that mints a user session.

The refresh token is intentionally absent: it is delivered as an ``HttpOnly``
cookie (see :mod:`yupay.modules.auth.cookies`) so JS cannot read it. Only the
short-lived access token — which the browser needs to attach as a Bearer header
— is returned in the body.

yupay__modules__evidence__schemas__Order.title: OrderEventOut
yupay__modules__evidence__schemas__Order.description: One entry of the order's own timeline, replayed into the pack.
